My daughter is severely autistic and requires general anesthesia for dental procedures. We were instructed to arrive at 9:00 a.m., and because of the level of care she requires, two of my other children had to take time off work to help transport and support her throughout the appointment. We also drove one hour each way to the dental hospital because we trusted that they were prepared to care for her. We rearranged our entire day based on the hospital's instructions.
Instead, we were left waiting for hours with absolutely no clear timeline, no communication, and no regard for the fact that my daughter has severe autism and cannot tolerate prolonged waiting. She had been fasting since the previous evening, as instructed, meaning she went an extremely long time without food or water.
During the wait, I went to the front desk multiple times to ask when my daughter's procedure would finally take place because no one had updated us. I was told there was no estimated time, and that someone would go ask the dentist and come back with an update. No one ever returned. We were simply left sitting there. That alone confirmed how terrible the communication is at this hospital.
Rather than taking her back for the dental cleaning procedure, the dental hospital gave her what they described as half a doze of the general anesthesia simply to calm her down because they were nowhere near ready to perform the procedure. More than two hours later, the medication began wearing off. She became hungry, thirsty, frustrated, and aggressive—as anyone familiar with autism could have anticipated. We were confined to a tiny room for hours while she became increasingly distressed.
When we finally decided we had no choice but to leave, the staff suddenly began scrambling to find a dentist. Until that moment, it appeared there wasn't even a dentist available to perform the procedure. Staff members were running through the halls with walkie-talkies and even stopped us at the elevator as we were leaving, telling us, "things happen." That is not an acceptable response after making a disabled patient fast, sedating her, and leaving her waiting for hours without proper planning or communication.
The drive home was heartbreaking. We then had to endure another one-hour drive home, during which my daughter became so distressed from not having eaten or had anything to drink all day that she began physically hitting everyone in the car. The entire situation was completely avoidable. The moment we got home and she was finally able to eat and drink, she calmed down almost immediately. Her suffering today was unnecessary.
This experience showed a shocking lack of organization, communication, and respect for patients with special needs and their families. We trusted Saint Bernard Hospital with one of the most vulnerable members of our family, and they completely failed her.
To any parent of a child with special needs: stay away from Saint Bernard Hospital or their dental office and seek care elsewhere. No family should have to watch their child endure what ours did because of poor planning, disorganization, and a complete lack of communication. Based on our experience, I would never entrust my daughter to this hospital again.
